title: UniRank: End-to-End Domain-Specific Reranking of Hybrid Text-Image Candidates

problem.claim: Multimodal reranking is challenging when candidate sets contain hybrid text and image items because text rerankers favor text candidates over image candidates.

gap.claim: Existing VLM-based rerankers commonly convert all candidates to images, creating computational overhead, while open-source multimodal rerankers trained on general-domain data often underperform in domain-specific scenarios.

contributions.claim: UniRank is a VLM-based reranking framework that directly scores and orders hybrid text-image candidates without modality conversion.
UniRank includes instruction tuning for calibrated cross-modal relevance scoring and hard-negative-driven preference alignment with query-level policy optimization through RLHF.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on scientific literature retrieval and design patent search show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, with Recall@1 gains of 8.9% and 7.3%, respectively.

narrative_sequence.summary: Reranking is important in information retrieval pipelines.
Hybrid text-image candidate sets create multimodal reranking difficulty through a modality gap and biased cross-modal ranking.
VLMs help with cross-modal alignment, but existing approaches often encode text as images and general-domain training can limit domain-specific performance.
UniRank directly scores hybrid candidates and uses instruction tuning plus preference alignment for domain adaptation.
The authors report improvements on scientific literature retrieval and design patent search.
